title: Basic Authentication
definition: The simplest form of HTTP authentication where the client sends the raw username and password combined into a single Base64 encoded string within the HTTP Header.
simpleExplanation: You take `username:password`, mash them together, scramble the text slightly (Base64), and send it to the server on every single request. The server unscrambles it and checks the database.
realWorldExample: Often used for internal company tools, simple admin dashboards, or older legacy APIs where complex token systems are overkill.

basic: Does Base64 encoding encrypt the password so hackers can't read it??
intermediate: Because Basic Auth sends the actual password on every single request, what protocol is absolutely mandatory to prevent immediate hacking?

answers.question: Does Base64 encrypt?
answers.answer: NO! Base64 is NOT encryption, it is just encoding (like translating English to French). Anyone who intercepts the network request can instantly decode it and read the plaintext password.

answers.question: What is mandatory?
answers.answer: HTTPS (SSL/TLS). Because the password is sent in plaintext on every request, HTTPS is required to encrypt the entire network tunnel, keeping the password safe from network sniffers.
